rationale: bugs_open/445 Phase 5 — the archetype the bug was filed for, now designed from evidence rather than from three examples. Seven live sites resolved to magazine-grid on ONE shared tag at 7-10% coverage of their own declared identity; the terms they emit that NO layout could match were content-hub (3 of 7) and interactive-tools (2 of 7) — 'content hub with embedded tools', the same answer 445 §3 reached from an owner's eye, found independently in the sites' own vocabulary. This migration seeds that layout. The tag set was CHOSEN BY SIMULATION: four candidates scored against all 33 composed sites with a re-implemented scorer that reproduces the matcher's own recorded score on 29 of 30, and against a marked-[ASSUMED] proxy for the 17 unbuilt remakes. Candidate A (445's title words) rescued 4 of 7 and left designblog.co.uk — the site the owner complained about — at 6%; candidate B (A plus the FORM words the sites already emit: editorial-guides, long-form-content, research-publication, content-platform, guides) rescued 6 of 7 (designblog 7%→16%, apis.uk 9%→19%) and pulled in two non-cluster sites both judged correct (gamedesign.uk, a design-practice publication; farmerinsurance.uk, self-described 'editorial-guides, content-platform, interactive-calculators', sitting on industry-hub matching ZERO tags — its two industry-hub siblings do NOT move). C and D added nothing. oufe.com is not rescued under any candidate: its own tags lead with interactive-platform, so tool-portal wins it, defensibly. THE THING I MOST WANT CHALLENGED: (1) the migration carries an inline REACHABILITY GUARD — it refuses to seed a layout that fewer than 2 current classification specs can reach by tag, because 9 of the 18 existing layouts have ZERO sites emitting any of their tags (their tags name an industry; the classifier emits form words). This is Phase 4 of the plan in its minimal, per-migration form; the reusable assert_layout_reachable() function plus a pattern-check rule is deferred and stated as owed. Is an inline guard acceptable as the first instance, or should the function land first? (2) Data only, live on COMMIT — selection for sites that compose AFTER this changes (that is the point), sites already composed do not move (owner decision 2026-09-03: fix forward only). (3) The CSS is a new css_template following the renderer contract (no --section-* defaults; surface classes surface-coloured; var(--section-*, var(--color-*)) inheritance); it frames both the sibling-layout class contract AND the classes the live tool-list/guide-list/hero/featured-content/category-listing/faq components actually emit, since three of those carry no inline style. The visual grammar is deliberately not either sibling: one editorial spine, a 680px reading column (narrower than both), full-width TOOL SHELVES that interrupt the prose, an inline .tool-embed at reading width, a quiet category strip, 6px radius.

plan.summary: Seed layout content-hub-tools (category editorial, scheme light, 9 tags chosen by simulation) with a reachability guard that refuses an unreachable layout, a verify block that re-checks reachability at the live row, and a deactivate-not-delete rollback. Data only, live on COMMIT, no roll. Sites already composed do not move.

edits.rationale: The archetype itself. Tags are the FORM words the cluster sites already emit, so the layout is reachable by real vocabulary — 14 current classification specs emit at least one of them [MEASURED 2026-09-03]. Category stays 'editorial' so the category bonus ties with magazine-grid and the decision falls to tag fit, which is where the new layout is supposed to win.
edits.sketch: INSERT INTO layouts (name, display_name, description, category, industry_tags, scheme, structure_tokens, css_template, origin, is_active) VALUES ('content-hub-tools', 'Content Hub — Tools in Context', '…', 'editorial', ARRAY['content-hub','interactive-tools','editorial-publication','long-form','long-form-content','editorial-guides','guides','research-publication','content-platform'], 'light', '{…}'::jsonb, $LAYOUT$ … $LAYOUT$, 'seed', true) ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET …;

edits.rationale: Guard 1 — reachability. 9 of 18 existing layouts have zero sites emitting any of their tags; this migration refuses to be the tenth. Counts DISTINCT current classification specs whose industry_tags contain any of the new tags (raw, plus 'editorial' which canonicalises to editorial-publication), aborts below 2. Guard 2 — never overwrite a non-seed row of the same name.
edits.sketch: DO $$ … SELECT count(DISTINCT ss.site_id) INTO v_reach FROM site_specs ss, jsonb_array_elements_text(ss.data->'industry_tags') e(tag) WHERE ss.aspect='classification' AND ss.is_current AND e.tag = ANY(ARRAY[…]); IF v_reach < 2 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '736: only % current site(s) emit any of this layout''s tags — refusing to seed an unreachable layout'; END IF; … $$;

edits.rationale: Verify block using DO/RAISE (a verify block of SELECTs cannot stop the COMMIT under ON_ERROR_STOP). Asserts the row is active/light/editorial with exactly 9 tags, the CSS is not truncated, the template declares no --section-* default (renderer contract), and RE-CHECKS reachability against the seeded row's own industry_tags rather than a copy of the list.
edits.sketch: DO $$ … IF position('--section-text:' in css) > 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'renderer contract violated'; … SELECT count(DISTINCT ss.site_id) … JOIN layouts l ON l.name='content-hub-tools' WHERE e.tag = ANY(l.industry_tags) OR e.tag='editorial'; IF v_reach < 2 THEN RAISE …; $$;

edits.rationale: Deactivates rather than deletes: css_themes.layout_id → layouts is ON DELETE SET NULL, so a DELETE would silently null the layout on any site composed onto it since. Deactivation stops NEW compositions choosing it (the matcher reads is_active=true) and leaves composed sites rendering; a human decides about them.
edits.sketch: UPDATE layouts SET is_active=false, updated_at=NOW() WHERE name='content-hub-tools' AND origin='seed'; -- with a NOTICE naming how many sites keep it
